description: Capability for the DESKTOP native webview. The plugin builds a single `Window` (label 'native-webview') with two child webviews on desktop: 'native-webview-chrome' (a Tauri `about:blank` page that draws the host/subtitle/message + back/forward/refresh chrome bar) and 'native-webview-content' (the external URL with the caller's document-start script). Only 'native-webview-content' is granted here, and only `core:event:default` — so the browser-sniffer bridge transport can ride `BRIDGE_EVENT` from the loaded page (the event-bus-only posture the sniffer's now-removed top-level `WebviewWindow` capability used — this capability replaced it). The page is deliberately NOT granted `log:default`: this is untrusted remote content (`remote.urls` = `https://*`/`http://*`), and a direct log grant would let any third-party page write attacker-controlled lines into the host's log stream. Any diagnostics the page needs to surface must instead ride the event bus so the host wraps and controls them. 'native-webview-chrome' is intentionally absent: chrome → Rust IPC goes through a custom-scheme `on_navigation` intercept (no `__TAURI__` commands), and Rust → chrome state push uses `Webview::eval`, which is Rust-initiated and bypasses capability checks. `remote.urls` is required so IPC from the Origin::Remote external page isn't rejected. On iOS/Android the native webview is a separate WKWebView / android.webkit.WebView and this capability does not apply.
